# Education in Nigeria
Primary education in Nigeria typically begins around age 5 and lasts 6 years, culminating in a first school-leaving certificate. The curriculum includes core subjects such as Mathematics, English, Religious Knowledge, Agricultural Science, Home Economics, and one of the major indigenous languages (Hausa-Fulani, Yoruba, Igbo). The Universal Basic Education (UBE) program integrates 6 years of primary with 3 years of junior secondary education, establishing compulsory, free, and continuous schooling monitored by the Universal Basic Education Commission. Transition from primary to secondary education is automatic based on continuous assessment.
Secondary education spans junior and senior levels (3 years each) under a 9-3-4 or 6-3-3-4 system; students study core and elective subjects leading to the Senior Secondary Certificate Examination (SSCE) or General Certificate of Education (GCE). Admission into federal government colleges ("unity schools") is merit-based via national entrance exams, while many state-owned schools face challenges including staffing and funding shortages. Private secondary schools, though more expensive, offer smaller classes, better facilities, and qualified teachers. Vocational education is overseen by the National Board for Technical Education, but remains underdeveloped with many students engaged in informal apprenticeships. Despite numerous efforts, literacy rates remain unequal across regions and genders, though recent governmental initiatives aim to improve general and digital literacy, with a commitment to equitable access and focus on vulnerable populations such as girls and rural communities.
